metadata.title: SPARC Application Load Balancer Component Definition

components.title: AWS Application Load Balancer
components.description: Public-facing ALB with HTTPS listener (ACM certificate), HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, and IP-type target group for ECS Fargate tasks. Deployed via Terraform (AWS/ECS/modules/alb/). <!-- UPDATE: Insert ALB ARN, DNS name, ACM certificate ARN, and domain name for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for ALB

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity: All external client traffic is encrypted via TLS. The HTTPS listener on port 443 uses an ACM-managed certificate with TLS 1.3 policy (ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06). HTTP requests on port 80 receive a 301 redirect to HTTPS, ensuring no unencrypted client communication. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000062, CIS AWS 2.1.2.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: aws_lb_listener.https (TLS termination), aws_lb_listener.http_redirect (301 redirect). TLS policy enforces TLS 1.2 minimum with TLS 1.3 preferred.

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Cryptographic Protection: ALB uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for TLS certificate provisioning and automatic rotation. The ssl_policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 enforces strong cipher suites and disables deprecated protocols (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1). Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000014.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Certificate ARN is provided via the certificate_arn variable. ACM handles certificate renewal automatically.

implemented-requirements.description: Denial-of-Service Protection: AWS ALB provides built-in DDoS protection via AWS Shield Standard (included at no cost). The ALB distributes incoming traffic across multiple ECS tasks in private subnets, preventing single-point-of-failure. Consider adding AWS WAF for application-layer protection. Reference: CIS AWS 6.1.
implemented-requirements.remarks: For enhanced protection, attach AWS WAF WebACL and enable AWS Shield Advanced.

implemented-requirements.description: Remote Access: The ALB serves as the sole ingress point for remote user access to the application. All remote sessions are encrypted via TLS. The ALB security group restricts inbound traffic to ports 80 and 443 only. Backend ECS tasks are not directly accessible from the internet. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000015.
implemented-requirements.remarks: ALB is deployed in public subnets; ECS tasks are in private subnets with no public IP.

implemented-requirements.description: Information Input Validation: ALB health checks validate application availability by checking the /nginx-health endpoint on the NGINX sidecar container. This lightweight endpoint returns HTTP 200 without proxying to Rails, verifying that the reverse proxy layer is functional. Unhealthy targets are automatically removed from the target group rotation. The ALB routes to the NGINX container (port 8080), which then proxies to Rails (port 3000 on localhost).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Health check settings: interval=30s, healthy_threshold=3, unhealthy_threshold=3, timeout=5s, matcher=200, path=/nginx-health. ALB target group uses IP type (Fargate requirement) and targets the NGINX container.

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary Protection: The ALB drops invalid HTTP headers (drop_invalid_header_fields=true), preventing header injection attacks from reaching backend services. Deletion protection is enabled (enable_deletion_protection=true), preventing accidental or unauthorized removal of the network boundary. Access logging is configurable via an S3 bucket for forensic analysis of all requests. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000364. AWS WAFv2 (SC-7 edge inspection, #578): a regional web ACL is associated with the ALB and inspects every inbound request before it reaches the backend. AWS-managed rule groups block known-bad inputs (incl. Log4Shell / CVE-2021-44228) and known-malicious source IPs (Amazon IP-reputation list) immediately; the CommonRuleSet and SQLi groups are BLOCK in prod (waf_block_mode=true, enforcing from deployment; the module retains a COUNT capability for other environments to observe first). One permanent per-rule exception (#609): CommonRuleSet's SizeRestrictions_BODY is overridden to COUNT, because it rejects any request body over 8 KB — WAF's body-inspection ceiling for a REGIONAL web ACL — which blocks every legitimate compliance-artifact upload while adding no inspection coverage, as WAF cannot inspect beyond that ceiling regardless of action. Request-size enforcement is therefore performed at the reverse proxy (nginx client_max_body_size 110m) and in application-layer upload validation, not at the web ACL. All other CommonRuleSet rules remain enforcing. A rate-based rule throttles L7 floods per source IP. Scope-down exception (#620): the CommonRuleSet group (priority 1) does NOT evaluate write requests (POST/PATCH/PUT) to the seven artifact-upload path families (/evidences, /ssp_documents, /sar_documents, /sap_documents, /poam_documents, /profile_documents, /cdef_documents). Rationale: uploaded evidence is arbitrary binary and document content (PDF, DOCX, JPEG, XML, JSON, YAML) whose bytes match XSS and SQLi signatures by coincidence; CrossSiteScripting_BODY blocked a legitimate 34 KB evidence upload on 2026-08-03 with no application-layer trace. The exception is scoped to that ONE rule group and to write methods only: KnownBadInputs (priority 2), SQLi (priority 3), the Amazon IP-reputation list (priority 4) and the rate-based rule (priority 0) are each separate top-level rules and continue to evaluate these paths unchanged, as does CommonRuleSet on GET requests to the same paths. Content validation for uploads is enforced at the application layer, which is the only layer able to decode a multipart body and check declared file type; WAF inspects at most the first 8 KB of any body on a REGIONAL web ACL. Path-scoped rather than content-type-scoped deliberately: exempting multipart/form-data globally would let an attacker bypass CommonRuleSet on any endpoint by setting that header. These endpoints additionally require an authenticated application session.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resource: aws_lb.main with drop_invalid_header_fields=true, enable_deletion_protection=true, access_logs block.

implemented-requirements.description: Information System Monitoring: the ALB WAFv2 web ACL emits sampled request logs and per-rule CloudWatch metrics (#578). WAF logs are delivered to a dedicated CMK-encrypted CloudWatch log group (aws-waf-logs-*, 365-day retention) with Authorization and Cookie headers redacted. Blocked/counted matches are visible for detection and false-positive review, and a blocked-request metric supports alerting. Rules overridden to COUNT retain full detection value: a counted match still emits its rule label (e.g. awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:SizeRestrictions_Body, #609) to the WAF log, so oversize-body traffic remains queryable for anomaly review even though it is not blocked at the edge. Note for audit: a request terminated at the web ACL never reaches the application, so it produces no application-layer audit event (AU-2/AU-12) — WAF logs are the sole record of edge-blocked requests. Scope-down exception telemetry (#620): requests exempted from CommonRuleSet by the upload-path scope-down are still logged by the web ACL and still evaluated by the other three managed rule groups and the rate-based rule, so their matches remain visible in the WAF logs. A scope-down differs from a rule override in that the excluded requests emit no CommonRuleSet rule labels at all — detection for that group is forgone on those paths, not merely un-enforced. Upload anomaly detection on those paths therefore relies on the remaining rule groups plus application-layer audit events, which DO exist for these requests because they now reach the application.
